In detail

This is the sector every list of “neighbourhoods to avoid in Bucharest” is written about, because Ferentari and Rahova are in it. The police's own table does not support that ranking: Sector 5 scored 94.84 in 2025, below Sector 2 (112.70), Sector 6 (111.53) and Sector 3 (106.65) — below three sectors nobody writes lists about. The figures are the Bucharest Police's own published “coefficient of specific criminality” by sector, 2014-2025. The force does not state what the coefficient is per, so it is used here to compare sectors against each other and against their own past, which is what it supports, and not read as a rate per head. Two honest qualifications. The coefficient is a sector average and Ferentari is a small, poor part of a sector that also contains Cotroceni and the presidential palace, so it cannot tell you about one street. And the trend is the steepest in the city: 68.71 in 2023, 82.90 in 2024, 94.84 in 2025. A sociologist quoted by Digi24 on Bucharest's “fear map” argues the reputation is socioeconomic labelling rather than measurement. Visitors have no reason to be in Ferentari either way.
